## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag needs to take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's CLI-flag policy requires this for every new flag under `cli/`, and CI sets options through the environment.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` option that `collect` uses to skip files whose basename matches any pattern, and logs each skipped path. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md` and adds parser, `collect` and end-to-end archive tests, plus a text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Default `--exclude` from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` — When CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log`, nothing is excluded, because the flag uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. This breaks `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment silently get archives that still contain the files they meant to exclude. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")` (split into a list using a documented separator), document the variable in `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment-set case.
